teams.heading: Italy captain Nicotera rates Fiji more manageable, but warns of individual brilliance
teams.body: Speaking to the media in his pre-match press conference, Italy hooker and captain Giacomo Nicotera said the world rankings reflect real gaps between sides. He also cautioned that Fiji remain a team to fear, pointing to their incredible individual talent and their players in France's Top 14. The Azzurri go into Saturday's Round 6 test still chasing a first win of the tournament after defeats to South Africa (7-66) and Argentina (14-19). Fiji arrive bottom of the log, beaten in all five matches, most recently 15-43 by Ireland.

lead.why: It is the only new item: the Italy captain's assessment of Fiji on the eve of the Round 6 test.

teams.heading: BBC credits Will Stuart's Achilles comeback with reviving England's attacking swagger
teams.body: BBC Sport's Mike Henson ties England's revival to Will Stuart, the England and British and Irish Lions star who missed the start of the year with a ruptured Achilles tendon. Without him England endured a terrible Six Nations and five straight defeats. Since his return they have scored 20 tries against Australia and Japan and rank top of the Nations Championship for points scored and entries into the opposition 22. New Zealand arrive at Twickenham on Saturday stung by last weekend's 35-28 defeat to Wales.

lead.why: A fresh England player storyline, Stuart's return and the attack's revival, distinct from the Itoje and Borthwick editions already run.

teams.heading: Fabien Galthié defends referees after Rassie Erasmus's six-match ban for match-fixing claim
teams.body: France head coach Fabien Galthié said on Thursday coaches have a duty to protect referees. He did so without naming Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus, banned for six matches for suggesting officials' failure to punish knee-drop tackles in France's 21-19 win in Paris amounted to “manipulation” or “match-fixing”. “If I don't take care with the words I use when discussing refereeing, I can cause harm to rugby, the supporters and our opponents,” he said. Since 2020, he added, he has backed officials whatever the result, airing disagreements only with those who manage the laws.

lead.why: France's own head coach publicly addressing the Erasmus refereeing row is fresh France news; the Jelonch story has already led today.

teams.heading: Concussed Sam Illo out as Thomas Clarkson joins Ireland bench against Springboks
teams.body: Connacht tighthead prop Sam Illo failed to complete return-to-play protocols after the concussion he picked up in last week's 43-15 win over Fiji, forcing Ireland head coach Andy Farrell into a late change for Saturday's Nations Championship test against South Africa at the Aviva Stadium, SA Rugby Magazine reports. Leinster's Thomas Clarkson takes the No. 18 jersey and is in line for his first appearance of the championship's second leg, while Connacht's Finlay Bealham has joined the squad as emergency cover.

lead.why: A late injury-forced change to Ireland's matchday 23 is fresh hard news about Ireland's own team.

teams.heading: Captain Giacomo Nicotera says Italy carry lingering frustration into Udine Fiji test
teams.body: In his pre-match press conference, Italy captain Giacomo Nicotera said the side could not be satisfied with the 14-19 Round 5 defeat to Argentina. He added that they want to show they are the Italy capable of great feats rather than the team of recent weeks. The Trieste native called Fiji, Saturday's visitors to Udine, more beatable, in line with the world rankings, but still a side to fear for their individual talent. He also said debutant fly-half Domingo Miotti had settled in very well.

lead.why: The captain's eve-of-match comments are the freshest Italy story not yet run; the selection story has already led.

teams.heading: Rory Darge's shoulder injury hands Stafford McDowall the Scotland captaincy against Japan
teams.body: Glasgow Warriors openside Rory Darge, man of the match against Australia, was initially named to start despite a shoulder injury, but after further assessment he will sit out the Japan test at Murrayfield. It is head coach Gregor Townsend's second change of captain in a week, after Sione Tuipulotu was ruled out. Centre Stafford McDowall, called in from his father's farm in Dumfries to come off the bench against the Wallabies, takes the armband. Matt Fagerson starts at No. 8, with Ollie Leatherbarrow moving to openside.

lead.why: The U20 win has already run, so the top new senior story is the late loss of captain Rory Darge and the back-row reshuffle for Japan.

teams.heading: Tomos Williams credits Prem for Wales confidence as nine England-based players start
teams.body: Saracens scrum-half Tomos Williams told BBC Sport that life in England's Prem has changed the mindset of Welsh players, saying English players carry more confidence and "Boys realise that they're not a million miles better than us." He is one of nine England-based players in Wales head coach Steve Tandy's side for Saturday's Nations Championship Test v Australia in Cardiff, including the entire front row, while Exeter's Kane James is among the replacements and set for his first home Test appearance.

lead.why: It is the freshest Wales-team story not yet run, and it rests on today's selection facts for the Australia Test.

teams.heading: Facundo Isa handed Pumas No. 8 shirt for first start since 2025
teams.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi has promoted the Pau No. 8 from the bench in Genoa to start Saturday's test against France. It is one of seven changes that restore Julián Montoya as captain and Tomás Lavanini to the second row. Isa, who put his international career on hold in 2023, last started for the Pumas in July 2025's defeat to England. He has started seven of nine club matches this season, including a brace against Toulouse on 1 November. Club coach Sébastien Piqueronies notes he is out of contract.

lead.why: The Montpellier row has already run and Laporte's reply only continues it, so Isa's recall to the starting XV is the freshest Argentina selection news.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson says dry Cardiff roof gives Wallabies licence to attack
teams.body: Wallabies captain Harry Wilson expects Cardiff's Principality Stadium roof to free the attack that stalled in Murrayfield's drizzle. By his account, the 12-15 loss to Scotland was little more than box kicks and chasing scraps. For Saturday's test against Wales, "dry conditions, we really have a licence to back our game," he said, name-checking Tom Hooper and Carlo Tizzano, promoted to the starting pack alongside a front row lifted from the bench. Wales arrive buoyed by last weekend's 35-28 win over the All Blacks.

lead.why: It is the only new Australia story, with the Wallabies captain setting out the plan for the Wales test.

teams.heading: Japan call up Taufa Latu as props Tamafusa and Helu miss Scotland
teams.body: Keijiro Tamafusa and Opeti Helu are both missing from Japan's front row for Saturday's Nations Championship test against Scotland, Rugby Asia 247 reports, with Shuhei Takeuchi and Riku Tokito also absent through injury or conditioning. Toyota Verblitz's Taufa Latu is among the call-ups. It is a thin hand to bring to Murrayfield after the 78-15 hammering by England, against a Scotland side who edged Australia 15-12 last weekend and have won eight of nine previous meetings.

lead.why: Japan's absences and call-ups are fresh hard team news, distinct from the Riley and Townsend stories already run.

teams.heading: NZR chair David Kirk warns 'serious examination' awaits poor All Blacks display
teams.body: The NZ Rugby chair said he would be "pretty disappointed" by defeat in Saturday's test against England at Twickenham. He cautioned against judging the side on the result alone, since it could lose while playing well. The scrutiny on head coach Dave Rennie follows last weekend's 35-28 loss to Wales, New Zealand's first defeat by the Welsh in 73 years. Kirk called that result a "miracle" for Wales. He also cited three defeats by the Springboks in what he called the All Blacks' "hardest year."

lead.why: The NZ Rugby chair putting the All Blacks on notice before Twickenham is fresh, hard pressure on Rennie's side.

teams.heading: Springbok assistant Mzwandile Stick says Prendergast would be banned if Fijian
teams.body: Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast was cleared by an independent panel over an alleged hip-drop tackle on Fiji's Peceli Yato and is free to face the Springboks on Saturday. Stick, South Africa's assistant coach, was unimpressed on Friday: "If that was a Fijian player, he would be sitting in Fiji now doing some extra lessons of how to tackle." He also demanded World Rugby clarify the new hip-drop tackle law, echoing banned head coach Rassie Erasmus's claim that 17 knee-drop tackles went unpunished against France.

lead.why: Stick's Friday barb about Prendergast's cleared citing is the freshest South Africa event and the line fans are quoting before the Ireland test.
